s81.content:
A wealthy lawyer and teacher of rhetoric who converted in middle age, Cyprian became bishop of Carthage soon after. He guided his Church through the Decian persecution and a devastating plague, and wrote influential works on the unity of the Church.

He is known for the line "He cannot have God for his Father who does not have the Church for his mother." He was beheaded during the persecution of Valerian and shares his feast with his friend Pope St. Cornelius.
s81.intercession: St. Cyprian, shepherd in time of persecution and plague, pray for the Church. Keep us united in faith and charity, and faithful in every trial. Amen.

s82.content:
The mother of Emperor Constantine, Helena became a Christian later in life. In her late seventies she made a pilgrimage to the Holy Land, where she founded churches at Bethlehem and on the Mount of Olives.

Tradition credits her with discovering the True Cross in Jerusalem, near the site where the Church of the Holy Sepulchre was then built. She is a patron of converts, archaeologists, and difficult marriages.
s82.intercession: St. Helena, who sought the Cross of Christ, pray for us. Help us to embrace the crosses of our own lives and to find in them the love that saves the world. Amen.

s83.content:
As a young deacon, Athanasius attended the Council of Nicaea, and as bishop of Alexandria he spent the rest of his life defending its teaching that Christ is truly God. He was exiled five times by emperors sympathetic to Arianism, spending some seventeen years in exile.

His works include On the Incarnation and a Life of St. Anthony that spread the monastic ideal across the Christian world. The phrase "Athanasius against the world" came to describe his lonely stand for orthodoxy.
s83.intercession: St. Athanasius, defender of the divinity of Christ, pray for us. Help us to hold fast to the true faith when it is unpopular, and to love the Word made flesh with all our hearts. Amen.

s84.content:
A deacon from Nisibis in Mesopotamia, Ephrem wrote hundreds of hymns and poems teaching the faith, earning him the title "Harp of the Holy Spirit." He used choirs of women to sing his hymns, which countered heretical songs popular at the time.

He spent his last years in Edessa and died after caring for victims of a famine and plague. Pope Benedict XV declared him a Doctor of the Church in 1920.
s84.intercession: St. Ephrem, Harp of the Holy Spirit, pray for us. Teach us to praise God with our whole being and to find beauty in the truths of our faith. Amen.

s85.content:
A Roman soldier from Pannonia, Martin met a freezing beggar at the gates of Amiens, cut his military cloak in half with his sword, and gave half away. That night he dreamed of Christ wearing the half-cloak. He was soon baptized and left the army.

He founded one of the first monasteries in Gaul and was acclaimed bishop of Tours by the people against his will. He is a patron of soldiers, of the poor, and of France.
s85.intercession: St. Martin of Tours, who clothed Christ in the beggar, pray for us. Open our eyes to see the Lord in the poor, and give us generous hands to share what we have. Amen.

s86.content:
One of the three Cappadocian Fathers, Basil was bishop of Caesarea and a key defender of the Nicene faith, especially of the divinity of the Holy Spirit. His Rule shaped Eastern monasticism, and he founded a vast complex that included a hospital, a hostel, and a poorhouse.

The Divine Liturgy of St. Basil is still celebrated in the Eastern Churches. He shares his feast with his lifelong friend St. Gregory of Nazianzus.
s86.intercession: St. Basil, pastor, monk, and friend of the poor, pray for us. Teach us to join prayer and work, contemplation and charity, in lives given wholly to God. Amen.

s87.content:
Called "the Theologian" in the East, Gregory was a poet and preacher who loved solitude but was repeatedly drawn into Church leadership. As bishop of Constantinople he preached five Theological Orations on the Trinity that helped shape the Council of Constantinople in 381.

He resigned the see amid controversy and retired to write poetry and prayer. He shares his feast day with St. Basil, his close friend since their student days in Athens.
s87.intercession: St. Gregory the Theologian, pray for us. Help us to contemplate the mystery of the Holy Trinity with reverence and to speak of God with both truth and love. Amen.

s88.content:
So gifted a preacher that he was later called Chrysostom, "golden-mouthed," John was a priest of Antioch before becoming archbishop of Constantinople. His homilies on Scripture remain classics, and he denounced the luxury of the rich while the poor went hungry.

His criticism of the imperial court led to his exile, and he died on a forced march in 407. The Divine Liturgy most often celebrated in the Byzantine Churches bears his name. He is a patron of preachers.
s88.intercession: St. John Chrysostom, golden-mouthed preacher, pray for us. Give preachers courage and eloquence, and give all of us hearts that hear the Word and do it. Amen.

s89.content:
Patriarch of Alexandria, Cyril led the defense of the unity of Christ’s person against Nestorius, who denied that Mary could rightly be called Theotokos, "God-bearer." He presided over the Council of Ephesus in 431, which affirmed the title.

A forceful and at times controversial leader, Cyril was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1882 for his theology of the Incarnation.
s89.intercession: St. Cyril, defender of the Mother of God, pray for us. Help us to adore Christ, true God and true man, and to honor Mary as his Mother and ours. Amen.

s90.content:
Pope from 440 to 461, Leo was one of the most important early popes. His Tome, a letter setting out the doctrine of Christ’s two natures in one person, was acclaimed at the Council of Chalcedon with the cry "Peter has spoken through Leo."

In 452 he met Attila the Hun near Mantua and persuaded him to turn back from Rome, and in 455 he limited the Vandals’ sack of the city. His sermons are still read in the Liturgy of the Hours.
s90.intercession: Pope St. Leo, shepherd and teacher, pray for the Church. Strengthen the Pope and all bishops to proclaim the faith clearly and to protect their flocks. Amen.

s91.content:
Consecrated to God as a girl, Genevieve lived a life of prayer and fasting in Paris. When Attila’s army approached in 451, she urged the people to pray rather than flee, and the city was spared.

During a later siege by the Franks she led a convoy to bring grain to the starving city, and she persuaded King Clovis to show mercy to prisoners. She is the patron saint of Paris.
s91.intercession: St. Genevieve, protector of Paris, pray for our cities. Teach us to trust in prayer in times of danger and to care for our neighbors in need. Amen.

s92.content:
One of Ireland’s three patron saints with Patrick and Columba, Brigid founded a double monastery at Kildare that became a great center of learning and art. Countless stories celebrate her boundless generosity to the poor.

The woven St. Brigid’s cross, made from rushes, is still hung in Irish homes for protection. Since 2023, her feast has been a public holiday in Ireland.
s92.intercession: St. Brigid, Mary of the Gael, pray for us. Make our homes places of welcome and our hands generous to the poor, and kindle in us the fire of God’s love. Amen.

s93.content:
The twin sister of St. Benedict, Scholastica led a community of consecrated women near Monte Cassino. St. Gregory the Great tells how, at their last meeting, she asked Benedict to stay and talk through the night; when he refused, she prayed, and a violent storm kept him from leaving.

She died three days later, and Benedict saw her soul rise to heaven as a dove. The siblings are buried in the same tomb.
s93.intercession: St. Scholastica, who loved much and so could do more, pray for us. Teach us the power of confident prayer and the joy of holy friendship. Amen.

s94.content:
An Irish monk of royal lineage, Columba (Colmcille) founded monasteries across Ireland before leaving for Scotland around 563, possibly in penance for a dispute that ended in battle. He founded the monastery on the island of Iona.

Iona became a center for the evangelization of the Picts and northern England, and a great school of learning. He is one of the three patron saints of Ireland.
s94.intercession: St. Columba, pilgrim for Christ, pray for us. Help us to turn our failings into occasions of grace and to carry the Gospel wherever God sends us. Amen.

s95.content:
A Roman prefect who became a monk, Gregory was elected pope in 590 during plague and war. He organized famine relief, negotiated with the Lombards, and in 597 sent St. Augustine of Canterbury and forty monks to evangelize the English.

His Pastoral Rule guided bishops for centuries, and he called himself "the servant of the servants of God," a title popes still use. Gregorian chant bears his name. He is a patron of musicians and teachers.
s95.intercession: Pope St. Gregory the Great, servant of the servants of God, pray for the Church. Give our shepherds wisdom and humility, and fill our worship with beauty. Amen.

s96.content:
Archbishop of Seville for over thirty years, Isidore worked to convert the Visigoths from Arianism and to strengthen the Church in Spain. His Etymologies, an encyclopedia of the knowledge of his age, was one of the most widely used books of the Middle Ages.

Because he sought to gather and organize all knowledge, he is popularly proposed as a patron of the internet and of computer users.
s96.intercession: St. Isidore, lover of learning, pray for us. Help us to use knowledge and technology wisely, for the good of others and the glory of God. Amen.

s97.content:
According to tradition, Dymphna was the daughter of a pagan Irish king and a Christian mother. After her mother’s death, her grief-stricken father sought to marry her, and she fled to Geel in present-day Belgium, where he found and killed her.

Geel became a place of pilgrimage for people with mental illness, and for centuries the town has welcomed them into family homes. She is the patron saint of those suffering from anxiety, depression, and mental illness.
s97.intercession: St. Dymphna, pray for all who suffer from mental illness, anxiety, and depression. Bring them peace, healing, and people who will walk beside them with patience and love. Amen.

s98.content:
Placed in the monastery of Wearmouth-Jarrow at age seven, Bede spent his entire life there studying, teaching, and writing. His Ecclesiastical History of the English People earned him the title "Father of English History."

He also popularized dating years from the birth of Christ (Anno Domini). He died on the eve of the Ascension while dictating a translation of John’s Gospel. He is the only English Doctor of the Church.
s98.intercession: St. Bede, faithful scholar, pray for us. Help us to love truth and learning and to offer all our work to God. Amen.

s99.content:
An English Benedictine monk named Wynfrith, Boniface was sent by the pope to evangelize the Germanic peoples. According to a famous story, he felled the sacred oak of Thor at Geismar, and when no harm came to him, many were converted.

He organized the Church in Germany and founded the abbey of Fulda. In his late seventies he was killed by bandits in Frisia while preparing to confirm new Christians. He is the patron of Germany.
s99.intercession: St. Boniface, apostle of Germany, pray for us. Give us courage to cast down the idols of our age and to build up the Church with patience. Amen.

s100.content:
Brothers from Thessalonica, Cyril and Methodius were sent in 863 to evangelize the Slavic peoples of Moravia. They created an alphabet for the Slavonic language, translated Scripture and the liturgy, and celebrated Mass in the people’s own tongue.

Their work laid the foundation of Slavic Christianity and culture, and the Cyrillic alphabet is named for Cyril. In 1980 Pope John Paul II named them co-patrons of Europe.
s100.intercession: Sts. Cyril and Methodius, apostles to the Slavs, pray for us. Help the Church to proclaim the Gospel in every language and culture, and to be one. Amen.

s101.content:
Duke of Bohemia, Wenceslaus was raised as a Christian by his grandmother St. Ludmila. He ruled with justice and was known for his charity to the poor, the widowed, and prisoners.

He was murdered by his brother Boleslaus on the way to Mass. Venerated as a martyr soon after, he is the patron saint of the Czech people, remembered in English as "Good King Wenceslas" of the Christmas carol.
s101.intercession: St. Wenceslaus, pray for all who govern. Help them to rule with justice and mercy and to care for the poor above all. Amen.

s102.content:
A renowned teacher at the cathedral school of Reims, Bruno left his career and, with six companions, withdrew to the mountains near Grenoble in 1084. There he founded the Grande Chartreuse and the Carthusian order, which combines solitary life with community.

The Carthusians have never been reformed, since they never needed reforming. Bruno spent his last years in a hermitage in Calabria.
s102.intercession: St. Bruno, lover of silence, pray for us. In a noisy world, help us to find time for stillness where God can speak to our hearts. Amen.

s103.content:
An English princess raised in exile in Hungary, Margaret married King Malcolm III of Scotland. She raised eight children, reformed Church practice in Scotland, founded churches, and restored the monastery of Iona.

She fed poor people and orphans at her own table each day and washed the feet of the poor. She is a patron of Scotland, of mothers, and of large families.
s103.intercession: St. Margaret of Scotland, queen and mother, pray for us. Help parents to form their children in faith and to open their homes to the poor. Amen.

s104.content:
An Italian who became abbot of Bec in Normandy and later archbishop of Canterbury, Anselm is called the "Father of Scholasticism." He described theology as "faith seeking understanding."

His Proslogion introduced the ontological argument for God’s existence, and his Why God Became Man shaped Western thought about the Atonement. As archbishop he defended the Church’s freedom from royal control and was twice exiled.
s104.intercession: St. Anselm, who taught us faith seeking understanding, pray for us. Help us to love God with our minds as well as our hearts. Amen.

s105.content:
A worldly cleric at the imperial court, Norbert converted after being thrown from his horse during a storm. He became an itinerant preacher and in 1120 founded the Canons Regular of Prémontré (the Norbertines), combining monastic life with pastoral work.

As archbishop of Magdeburg he reformed the clergy and was known for his devotion to the Eucharist.
s105.intercession: St. Norbert, pray for us. Deepen our love for Christ in the Eucharist and help us to turn back to God whenever we have strayed. Amen.

s106.content:
Bernard entered the new monastery of Cîteaux with some thirty relatives and friends, and at 25 was sent to found Clairvaux. He became the most influential churchman of his age, advising popes and kings and helping the Cistercian order spread across Europe.

His sermons on the Song of Songs and his devotion to the Virgin Mary earned him the title "Mellifluous Doctor," the honey-sweet teacher. The Memorare is traditionally attributed to him.
s106.intercession: St. Bernard, lover of Christ and Mary, pray for us. Help us to look to the Star, call upon Mary, and never despair of God’s mercy. Amen.

s107.content:
Chancellor of England and a close friend of King Henry II, Thomas was made archbishop of Canterbury in 1162. To the king’s dismay, he became a strict defender of the Church’s rights and lived austerely.

After years of conflict and exile, he was murdered in his cathedral by four of the king’s knights. His tomb at Canterbury became one of Europe’s great pilgrimage sites, the destination of the pilgrims in Chaucer’s Canterbury Tales.
s107.intercession: St. Thomas Becket, who stood for the freedom of the Church, pray for us. Give us courage to put God before every earthly power. Amen.

s108.content:
Inspired by the preaching of St. Francis, Clare left her noble family at eighteen to embrace poverty. She founded the Order of Poor Ladies, now the Poor Clares, at San Damiano, and led it for forty years.

She fought to secure the "privilege of poverty" and was the first woman to write a rule for religious women. When she was too ill to attend Mass, she saw it projected on her wall, and in 1958 she was named patron of television.
s108.intercession: St. Clare, radiant light of Christ, pray for us. Help us to gaze upon the Lord, to love poverty of spirit, and to trust him in all things. Amen.

s109.content:
A Hungarian princess married to Louis of Thuringia, Elizabeth used her position to serve the poor, distributing bread and building a hospital. A famous legend says bread she was secretly carrying to the poor turned to roses.

After her husband’s death on crusade, she became a Franciscan tertiary and spent her remaining years caring for the sick. She died at 24 and was canonized just four years later.
s109.intercession: St. Elizabeth of Hungary, servant of the poor, pray for us. Give us compassionate hearts and busy hands in the service of those in need. Amen.

s110.content:
King of France from 1226, Louis was known for his justice, his personal piety, and his care for the poor, often feeding beggars at his own table. He built the Sainte-Chapelle in Paris to house the Crown of Thorns.

He led two crusades and died of illness in Tunis during the second. He is the only French king to be canonized, and cities such as St. Louis, Missouri bear his name.
s110.intercession: St. Louis, just and holy king, pray for all leaders. Help them to govern with justice, humility, and love for the poor. Amen.

s111.content:
A theologian at the University of Paris alongside his friend Thomas Aquinas, Bonaventure was elected minister general of the Franciscans in 1257 and guided the order through a difficult period. His Journey of the Mind into God is a classic of mystical theology.

He was made a cardinal and died during the Second Council of Lyon. He is called the "Seraphic Doctor."
s111.intercession: St. Bonaventure, Seraphic Doctor, pray for us. Help us to ascend to God through all that he has made and to unite knowledge with love. Amen.

s112.content:
A German Dominican, Albert wrote on nearly every field of knowledge: theology, philosophy, botany, zoology, astronomy, and chemistry. He was among the first medieval scholars to master Aristotle and taught St. Thomas Aquinas, whose genius he recognized early.

He served briefly as bishop of Regensburg before returning to teaching. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1931 and is the patron of scientists.
s112.intercession: St. Albert the Great, pray for all scientists and students. Help us to see that faith and reason are friends, and that all truth leads to God. Amen.

s113.content:
As a young man in Forlì, Peregrine struck St. Philip Benizi during a political riot, then repented and joined the Servite order. He was known for standing whenever possible as a penance.

When a cancerous growth on his leg was to be amputated, he prayed through the night before a crucifix and awoke healed. He is the patron saint of those suffering from cancer.
s113.intercession: St. Peregrine, pray for all who suffer from cancer. Obtain for them healing, courage, and peace, and comfort those who love and care for them. Amen.

s114.content:
A Roman noblewoman who wished to be a nun but married at thirteen, Frances served God as a wife and mother for forty years. She nursed the sick during plague and famine and was said to be guided by the visible presence of her guardian angel.

She founded a community of lay women, the Oblates of Tor de’ Specchi. Because her angel lit the road before her, she was named patron of automobile drivers in 1925.
s114.intercession: St. Frances of Rome, pray for us, especially for drivers and travelers. Help us to find God in the duties of family life and to listen to our guardian angels. Amen.

s115.content:
An Indigenous Mexican convert, Juan Diego Cuauhtlatoatzin saw the Virgin Mary on the hill of Tepeyac in December 1531. She asked him to have a church built there, and when the bishop asked for a sign, roses bloomed in winter.

When he opened his tilma to show the roses, the image of Our Lady of Guadalupe appeared on the cloth, which is still venerated in Mexico City. He was canonized in 2002 as the first Indigenous saint of the Americas.
s115.intercession: St. Juan Diego, humble messenger of Our Lady of Guadalupe, pray for us. Help us to trust Mary’s care, as you did, and to carry her message to others. Amen.

s116.content:
A lawyer, scholar, and author of Utopia, Thomas More rose to become Lord Chancellor of England. He was also a devoted husband and father who gave his daughters an education equal to any man’s.

When he refused to swear the oath acknowledging Henry VIII as head of the Church in England, he was imprisoned in the Tower and beheaded, saying he died "the king’s good servant, but God’s first." He shares his feast with St. John Fisher and is patron of lawyers and politicians.
s116.intercession: St. Thomas More, the king’s good servant but God’s first, pray for us. Give us integrity of conscience, a sense of humor, and courage to follow God above all. Amen.

s117.content:
Bishop of Rochester and chancellor of Cambridge University, John Fisher was a noted scholar and preacher. He opposed Henry VIII’s attempt to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon and refused to accept the king as supreme head of the Church.

While he was imprisoned in the Tower, the pope made him a cardinal; the king responded by having him beheaded. He was the only English bishop to resist.
s117.intercession: St. John Fisher, faithful bishop, pray for all pastors. Give them courage to defend the truth, even when they must stand alone. Amen.

s118.content:
A Spanish Carmelite friar, John joined St. Teresa of Ávila in reforming the Carmelite order. Opponents of the reform imprisoned him for nine months in a tiny cell in Toledo, where he composed some of the greatest poetry in the Spanish language.

His works, including Dark Night of the Soul and Ascent of Mount Carmel, describe the soul’s purification on the way to union with God. He is called the "Mystical Doctor."
s118.intercession: St. John of the Cross, guide through the dark night, pray for us. When God seems absent, help us to trust him, and lead us to union with his love. Amen.

s119.content:
An Italian Jesuit and cardinal, Robert Bellarmine was the leading Catholic theologian of the Counter-Reformation, known for clear, charitable debate. He wrote catechisms that were used for centuries.

He lived simply, gave much of his income to the poor, and is a patron of catechists. He was declared a Doctor of the Church in 1931.
s119.intercession: St. Robert Bellarmine, pray for us. Help us to know our faith well, to explain it with charity, and to live it simply. Amen.

s120.content:
A mercenary soldier and compulsive gambler, Camillus converted at 25 and, suffering from an incurable leg wound, began caring for patients at a hospital in Rome. Appalled at the neglect of the sick, he founded the Ministers of the Sick (Camillians).

His brothers wore a red cross on their habits and served on battlefields, a forerunner of the Red Cross. He is a patron of the sick, nurses, and hospitals.
s120.intercession: St. Camillus, servant of the sick, pray for all who are ill and all who care for them. Help us to see Christ in every patient and to serve with tenderness. Amen.
